# Reliability engine (pilot)

Turns failure modes and fault trees into the probability of each hazard's top event over the item life, and places
it in the tailored MIL-STD-882E probability bands (SUS-RISKDEF-001). Every hazard has a tree. Hardware causes are
quantified; software, human, environmental, interface and systematic causes are undeveloped events, traced to their
causal factor but never given a number.

```bash
python -m tools.reliability.build            # docs/wiki/Reliability-Pilot.md, rel-*.svg figures, safety/generated/reliability.json
python -m tools.reliability.build --check    # CI: fail if stale
python -m unittest discover -s tools/reliability/tests -t .
```

## Records

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `reliability/parts.yaml` | Parts (`PT-nnn`) and their failure modes (`PT-nnn-FMn`): kind, value, error factor, status, where a sourced value should come from |
| `reliability/parameters.yaml` | Shared tree parameters (joints, hoses, cells, check interval, beta factor) |
| `reliability/HAZ-xxx-nnn.yaml` | The fault trees (`FT-nnn`) of one hazard: its exposure key in the tailoring, the trees, and causal factors deliberately not modelled, with the reason |

A failure mode is `rate` (per operating hour), `cycle` (per cycle), `latent` (a dormant failure found only by a
check or a demand, λ τ / 2) or `demand` (per demand). `count` repeats an event or gate over identical copies; a
`common_cause` event is the beta-factor share of its modes; an `undeveloped` event names its nature, its causal
factor and, for software, its SSF. The engine checks that every causal factor of the hazard is in a tree or listed
under `not_modelled`. `engine.py` explains the arithmetic; `build.py` writes the outputs.

Each tree reports the quantified probability of its hardware-only cut sets (a lower bound), its mixed cut sets with
the probability of the hardware defence behind the software or human cause, and its single-point undeveloped causes.

## Rules

- Values come from public handbooks (MIL-HDBK-217F, NSWC-11, MIL-HDBK-338B), supplier data or field data. Until a
  value is sourced it carries `status: assumed`, and every result built from it is labelled illustrative.
- Results are analysis, not evidence. The engine never writes a probability into a hazard record; a result can
  inform a hazard's probability only through a review record by the safety lead (rule R13).
- The approach follows the structure of FASTER (failure modes, mission-profile failure rates, fault trees, Monte
  Carlo) but no code from it: FASTER is circuit-level, ISO 26262 and states a GPL licence.
